name: CHARMS-local coding items v1 (prompt layer of charms_local_dictionary_v1.json)
general_rules: Code only what the report and its supplementary material state; never fill from general knowledge or from what is usual for KNHANES. This is data extraction: record what the report says was done, not whether it was done well (risk of bias is assessed separately later).

status (whether the information is in the report): reported = stated (cite it); not_reported = nothing in the whole input states it; unclear = the report touches it but the exact value cannot be fixed from the text (cite what there is); not_applicable = the object of the item does not exist in this study by design (e.g. no validation dataset exists -> its sample size; outcome not time-to-event -> censoring; no classification at a threshold -> threshold). Not having done a step is NOT not_applicable: if the report states that a step was not done, or cited statements establish it by logic (e.g. 'participants with missing data were excluded' -> no imputation, complete-case; 'inputs were fixed before any model was fitted' -> no data-driven predictor selection), the status is reported with value 'not done (stated)' or 'not done (established: ...)'; if the report is silent about a step the study could have had, it is not_reported. The mere absence of a value is not such a statement: e.g. performance printed without CI or SD -> performance.uncertainty not_reported, not 'reported: none'. Status answers the item's core question (the first sentence of the item, or the part marked 'Core:'). When the core question is answered but a further detail the item asks for is missing (e.g. threshold method stated, threshold number not printed), status is reported and the missing detail is its own value entry with value 'not_reported'. When only a related fact is given but not what the core question asks (e.g. missing data mentioned, no amount), status is not_reported (or unclear) and the related fact goes in the rationale. For validation items: if any validation or test data exist (split sample, cross-validation, bootstrap, external), items about that validation are not not_applicable; e.g. a random split of the same data has no geographic or temporal separation -> reported 'none (random split of the same data)'. not_applicable only when the study has no validation or test data at all; then all validation items are not_applicable except validation.type, which is reported 'no validation (no validation or test data)' (kind judged) so that studies without validation can be counted. Partly missing values never change an answered item to not_reported: e.g. events printed by sex and the overall total not printed -> status reported, the sex-specific values printed and the total, if given, kind derived.

inconsistency (separate from status): none = no contradiction found; present = two places in the report give contradictory information about the same fact, object and condition (e.g. different CIs for the same model and dataset in a table and a figure; different names for the same split); uncertain = possibly contradictory but the places may refer to different objects. Notation (> vs >=) and rounding are not inconsistencies. Describe it in inconsistency_note (both places with IDs), else ''. An inconsistency never changes the status: printed values that disagree are still reported. Scope: the coded report is the included version. Text that the input itself marks as another version or as submission-system material (e.g. an 'Original Manuscript' block with an earlier abstract in a preprint server PDF, an earlier preprint version, cover letters, reviewer reports) is not part of it: do not code from it when the main text gives the fact, and differences between it and the main text are not inconsistencies (inconsistency none; mention it in the rationale). A count of predictors and a count of coefficients or encoded columns (dummy levels, design-matrix columns) are different objects: a difference between them is not an inconsistency (uncertain at most, when the report does not say how predictors were encoded). Record present only when the same variable, model, cohort or split and the same statistic or count, under the same condition, is reported differently (e.g. the same n=3,411 group called validation in the text and Train in a supplementary table). Not inconsistencies: notation or wording differences; using two names (test, validation) for one split when nothing else conflicts; numbers in different units (predictors vs coefficients or design-matrix columns, candidate vs final variables, union of tool inputs vs inputs of each model); different analyses (best model per cohort vs recommended final model; exclusion of some persons and imputation of others). Use uncertain only when the report does not allow telling whether two places refer to the same object.

No unsupported inference: never enter a number, procedure, split or timing that the report does not state. value_kind: printed (copied exactly from text, table cell or figure label - also percentages and counts), derived (you computed it from printed numbers; give the formula in rationale), judged (classification of printed text into the item's categories; one sentence why), approx (read off a figure, prefix ~). Status with derived numbers: if at least one of the item's numbers is printed, status is reported and numbers you add from printed ones (e.g. an overall total summed from printed sex-specific counts) are entries with kind derived; if none of the item's numbers is printed, a derived or approximate number never makes the status reported: status is not_reported (or unclear) and a derived number is given only where the item allows derived values; with no number and nothing to derive it from, not_reported. Never state an absence (e.g. 'no external data', 'no linkage', 'not done', 'whole dataset') unless the report states it; record only what is stated. A phrase like 'all the data were normalised' does not state when the step was done relative to the split: scope not_stated, quote the phrase in the rationale. A figure or table is coded as belonging to a model (e.g. a comparator logistic model) only if its title, legend or text says so. value kind is given per value entry (kind): one item can hold printed and derived numbers side by side (e.g. printed n per sex and a derived total). Linking statements: a step's data scope or procedure may be coded only when the cited statements together name that step and the data it used (e.g. CART predictors taken from the univariable results of Tables 1-2, which are computed on all 672 participants -> that step used the whole dataset). A general statement ('all preprocessing was fitted on the training set') does not fix the scope of a step it does not name (e.g. imputation listed elsewhere), and a table total alone does not show that a step used the whole sample before a split -> not_stated or unclear. kind: printed = text copied as is; when the value is a category of the item assigned from printed text (e.g. '10-fold cross-validation within the training set' -> within_cv_folds; 'nationwide longitudinal survey' -> cohort_study), kind is judged and the printed phrase follows the category.

Unit of extraction: each item says its unit (study, dataset, dataset/split, outcome, model, or evaluation = model x dataset). Give one value entry per unit the report distinguishes and name the unit as the report names it (e.g. 'XGBoost, KNHANES external set'); use unit '' for study-level items. Do not add subgroup entries unless the item's unit includes them. Unit label (canonical): the parts that apply, in this order, separated by ' | ': model | dataset or split | subgroup (e.g. 'CatBoost | KNHANES 2019 test | male'); names as the report gives them; 'all models' (or 'all datasets', 'both sexes') when the same value holds for every unit of that kind, and separate entries only where the values differ. Do not repeat performance rows (performance.estimate) in other items: give the metric names, counts or summary the item asks for.

evidence_ids: every ID you rely on (paragraph P0012, heading S02.01, cell T02-R05-C02, figure element, supplementary paragraph SUPTXT1.P3), copied exactly from the input; at least one for reported and unclear and for inconsistency present/uncertain. IDs not in the input are discarded.

Metrics: name metrics in normalised form followed by the printed name in parentheses when different: AUROC (AUC, ROC-AUC, C-statistic, area under the ROC curve), PR-AUC (AP, average precision, AUPRC), sensitivity (recall, TPR), specificity, PPV (precision), NPV, accuracy, balanced accuracy, F1, MCC, kappa, Brier score, log loss, calibration slope, calibration intercept, R2, RMSE, MAE, net benefit. A metric counts as reported only if a value is printed (table, text, or a value printed in a figure); figure axis labels (e.g. 'True Positive Rate', 'Precision') do not count. Metrics used only for predictor selection or tuning (e.g. LASSO binomial deviance/log loss, CV score used to pick hyperparameters) are not model performance.

Keep apparent (training), internal validation (split sample, cross-validation, bootstrap) and external validation results apart. A held-out split of the same data is never external validation. KNHANES used only for external evaluation counts as external. Cross-validation used only for tuning is recorded under tuning/resampling, not as the validation type of the reported estimates.

Keep apart (each has its own item): predictor availability at intended use; overlap between predictors and the outcome definition; which data each data-dependent step used (leakage-relevant facts); independence of validation data. Record facts in each; do not merge them into one judgement.
Copy printed text exactly; do not translate Korean; quote at most what is needed for the value. For definitions copy the defining phrase, not the whole sentence.

items.data_source.design: [unit: dataset] Source design of the data analysed (e.g. KNHANES cross-sectional national survey; cohort; registry; linked data). Value: short phrase per dataset.
items.data_source.setting: [unit: dataset] Type of setting in which the data were collected, as the report describes it: population_survey (national/community health survey) | hospital | clinic | registry | cohort_study | other, plus the printed phrase. The physical place of interviews/examinations (household, mobile examination centre) is not required; a description such as 'nationwide survey of noninstitutionalized Koreans' is reported. A survey that follows the same persons over waves (e.g. a nationally representative longitudinal study) is cohort_study; record national representativeness as an extra entry ('nationally representative').
items.data_source.geography: [unit: dataset] Country/region of the data (South Korea for KNHANES; any other country for other datasets). Value: list per dataset.
items.data_source.recruitment_dates: [unit: dataset] Calendar years/period of data collection used. Value: printed years per dataset.
items.data_source.survey_cycles: [unit: dataset] KNHANES cycles (I-IX) and/or survey years used, exactly as stated. Value: printed cycles/years; not_reported if only 'KNHANES' without years.
items.data_source.dataset_linkage: [unit: dataset] Core: whether data were pooled or linked to form an analysis dataset. Pooling = combining several survey years/cycles or several sources into one analysis dataset (e.g. 'KNHANES 2019-2021 pooled'); linkage = person-level record linkage to other data (questionnaire to registry, survey to claims). Value: what was pooled/linked, as printed. Using a separate dataset only for external validation, without combining it with the development data, is neither pooling nor linkage (it is recorded under validation items). Never write 'no linkage' unless stated; if the report describes no pooling or linkage, status not_reported. A conflict about survey years belongs to data_source.survey_cycles.
items.data_source.survey_design_weights: [unit: dataset] Whether the complex survey design (sampling weights, strata, clusters/PSU) was accounted for anywhere in the analysis, and how. Value: one of used_in_descriptive_only | used_in_model_development | used_in_evaluation | used_but_unclear_where | not_used_stated; plus printed detail. Class weights or loss weights for imbalance are not survey weights.
items.participants.eligibility: [unit: dataset] Inclusion criteria (age range, conditions, survey components required). Value: printed criteria.
items.participants.recruitment: [unit: dataset] How participants entered the data source as stated (survey sampling design such as stratified multistage probability sampling; consecutive patients; volunteers). For KNHANES: reported only if the report itself describes the sampling; the mere name KNHANES is not_reported. Inclusion of all eligible persons or records from a source (e.g. every eligible person's first test in a hospital laboratory system) is a stated entry method (reported); describe each dataset separately.
items.participants.exclusions: [unit: dataset] Exclusion criteria and the numbers excluded at each step where printed. Value: list {criterion, n}. Complete-case exclusion for missing data is listed here too (and in missing_data.exclusions).
items.participants.flow: [unit: study] Whether a participant flow (diagram or text with numbers from source population to analysed sample) is reported. Value: present (cite figure/paragraph) | absent.
items.participants.target_population: [unit: study] The population the model is intended for, as the report states it. Value: phrase.
items.sample_size.eligible_by_dataset: [unit: dataset/split] Number before exclusions (source population) per dataset. Value: printed n.
items.sample_size.analysed_by_dataset: [unit: dataset/split] Number analysed per dataset and per split (development/training, internal test, validation, external). Value: list {dataset/split, n} with printed n only; a split size computed from a ratio (e.g. 20% of 5,953) is not printed: status for that split not_reported (mention the derived figure in rationale only).
items.sample_size.events_nonevents: [unit: dataset/split] Numbers with and without the outcome per dataset/split. Value: list {dataset/split, events, nonevents}; printed preferred; derived allowed only from printed counts (formula in rationale; value_kind derived; status reported only if at least the events count is printed).
items.sample_size.outcome_prevalence: [unit: dataset/split] Outcome prevalence/proportion per dataset. Value: printed %, or derived from events/n.
items.sample_size.candidate_predictors_paramet: [unit: model; 'all models' when shared] Core: the number of candidate predictors considered and the number in the final model(s). Value entries '<unit> | candidate' and '<unit> | final' with the printed number, or 'not_reported' for the missing one; status reported when either number is printed (counting listed variables = kind derived). Domains or variable lists without counts are not counts: status not_reported unless the list can be counted (then derived).
items.sample_size.rationale: [unit: study] Any justification of the sample size (power, events per variable, Riley criteria). Value: printed statement or not_reported.
items.missing_data.amount_by_variable: [unit: dataset] Core: how much data are missing (overall or by variable). Value: printed numbers or percentages (or 'no missing data' when stated). If missing data are only mentioned (e.g. 'participants with missing values were excluded') without an amount, status not_reported; the exclusion belongs to missing_data.exclusions.
items.missing_data.exclusions: [unit: dataset] Core: whether participants with missing data were excluded (complete-case analysis). Value entries: 'excluded' = yes (stated) | no (stated) | not_stated; 'number excluded' = printed n or 'not_reported'.
items.missing_data.imputation_method: [unit: dataset] Imputation method (mean/median, MICE, kNN, missForest, model-native). Value: method name as printed.
items.missing_data.within_resampling_handling: [unit: dataset] Where imputation was fitted relative to the split/resampling, as stated: before_split (whole data) | training_only | within_cv_folds | not_stated; not_applicable if no imputation was done (stated complete-case analysis).
items.outcome.definition: [unit: outcome] Outcome definition including the variable, criterion/cutoff, classes or composite rule. Value: printed definition per outcome. List every outcome actually modelled, including outcomes of sensitivity or secondary analyses, labelled as such (e.g. 'log(urate), continuous - sensitivity analysis').
items.outcome.measurement: [unit: outcome] How the outcome was ascertained (measurement, questionnaire item, physician diagnosis, lab test). Value: printed.
items.outcome.timing_horizon: [unit: outcome] Time at which the outcome is defined relative to predictors (same survey = cross-sectional; follow-up horizon if prognostic). Value: cross_sectional | prognostic (horizon) | unclear.
items.outcome.assessors_blinding: [unit: outcome] Whether outcome assessment was blinded to predictors. For survey/lab outcomes usually not reported; do not assume. A checklist entry such as 'Not applicable (laboratory measurement)' is recorded as printed (status unclear) but does not establish that assessment was blinded.
items.outcome.censoring_follow_up: [unit: outcome] Follow-up and censoring handling for time-to-event outcomes; not_applicable for cross-sectional binary/continuous outcomes.
items.outcome.competing_risks: [unit: outcome] Competing risks handling for time-to-event outcomes; not_applicable otherwise.
items.predictors.definitions: [unit: study (or predictor group)] Whether candidate predictors are listed/defined. Value: listed_fully | listed_partly | not_listed, with where (table/paragraph IDs).
items.predictors.measurement_timing: [unit: study (or predictor group)] When predictors were measured relative to the outcome (same survey visit, earlier). Value: printed or judged.
items.predictors.availability_at_use: [unit: study, then predictor group] Only the inputs of the final model(s) offered for use (not all candidate predictors; candidates and their selection belong to predictors.definitions and predictors.selection). Value entries: 'intended setting' = the setting/time of use as stated, or 'not_stated'; then one entry per predictor group of the final model = how the values are obtained as stated or evident from the variable itself (body measurement, blood test, urine test, dietitian interview, ...), or 'not_stated' when the report does not say how a variable was collected (e.g. a diagnosis variable whose collection is not described; do not assume questionnaire). Do not judge yes/no availability: a predictor that needs a blood test is not 'unavailable', record 'blood test'. Do NOT judge here predictor-outcome overlap (predictors.outcome_overlap) or leakage (model_development.step_data_scope).
items.predictors.transformations: [unit: study (or predictor group)] Transformations, categorisation, scaling, encoding of predictors. Value: printed.
items.predictors.selection: [unit: study (or predictor group)] How predictors were chosen before modelling (literature, expert, univariable screening, all available). Value: printed.
items.model_development.model_family: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Algorithms developed/compared (as named in the report). Value: list of model names; mark the final/selected model if stated.
items.model_development.preprocessing: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Preprocessing steps (scaling, encoding, outlier handling, feature engineering). Value: printed list.
items.model_development.predictor_selection: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Feature selection within modelling (LASSO, RFE, Boruta, importance threshold, stepwise) and whether done on training data only. Value: method + where applied.
items.model_development.tuning_search: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Hyperparameter tuning (grid/random/Bayesian search, CV folds, defaults). Value: printed.
items.model_development.resampling: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Resampling used in development (k-fold CV, repeated CV, bootstrap) and for what. Value: printed.
items.model_development.class_imbalance: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Training-stage handling of class imbalance: SMOTE/ADASYN, over/undersampling, class or sample weights, threshold moving, and on which data it was applied (training only / whole data / not stated). Merging or redefining outcome classes is an outcome definition, not imbalance handling. 'not done (stated)' -> reported; silent -> not_reported.
items.model_development.survey_handling: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Whether survey weights/design entered model training or evaluation (sample weights in fitting, weighted metrics). Value: used_in_fitting | used_in_evaluation | not_used_stated | not_reported.
items.model_development.model_code_availabilit: [unit: model (or study when shared)] Whether code, model or data access is offered (repository link, 'available on request'). Value: printed statement.
items.validation.type: [unit: validation dataset / evaluation] Validation design of each reported performance evaluation (unit: evaluation = model x dataset): apparent | split_sample | cross_validation | bootstrap | temporal | geographic | fully_external. Value: list {evaluation, type}. Cross-validation used only inside training for tuning is not a validation type of the reported estimates (record it in tuning/resampling). If the study has no validation or test data at all: status reported, value 'no validation (no validation or test data)', kind judged (never not_applicable).
items.validation.split_resampling_units: [unit: validation dataset / evaluation] Split ratios / fold numbers / repeats and the unit split (person, survey year). Value: printed.
items.validation.geographic_temporal_separatio: [unit: validation or test dataset] Whether each validation/test dataset comes from another period or place than the development data. Value: 'temporal: <periods as printed>', 'geographic: <places as printed>', 'none (random split of the same data)' or 'none (cross-validation)' when the data are a random split or resampling of the development data, or 'not_stated'. not_applicable only when there is no validation or test data at all (see rule on validation items).
items.validation.independence: [unit: validation or test dataset] Two separate facts per validation/test dataset, as two value entries: '<dataset> | persons separate' = yes (stated, e.g. person-level split, different cohort) | no | not_stated; and '<dataset> | used for tuning or selection' = yes - what (hyperparameter tuning, choosing the algorithm or the number of predictors, threshold selection, recalibration or refitting, done on this dataset's outcomes before its performance was reported) | no (stated) | not_stated. E.g. separate hyperparameter tuning in each external cohort = yes; final algorithm chosen by its performance on the internal test set that also gives the reported estimate = yes; temporal test period patients included in earlier tuning = yes. Persons separate and used for tuning are independent facts; one never implies the other. A threshold chosen on this dataset whose threshold-dependent metrics are then reported on it = used for tuning or selection: yes - threshold selection. Persons of this dataset contained in data used earlier for tuning (e.g. temporal holdout period included in an earlier random-split training set used for hyperparameter tuning) = persons separate: no (in earlier tuning data), stated as such.
items.validation.sample_events: [unit: validation dataset / evaluation] Size and events of each validation set. Value: list {set, n, events}. For cross-validation the total sample that was cross-validated is not a validation set size: fold sizes/events only if printed, else not_reported (the total belongs to sample_size.analysed_by_dataset).
items.validation.updating_recalibration: [unit: validation dataset / evaluation] Model updating or recalibration before or at validation (unit: validation dataset). not_applicable only when no validation dataset exists; if validation exists and nothing is said about updating, not_reported; stated 'no recalibration' -> reported 'not done (stated)'. Per dataset, keep apart: model evaluated as developed without recalibration (stated); a recalibration or updating experiment; refitting for a temporal or other validation.
items.performance.metric_definition: [unit: study] Performance metrics with printed values (normalised name, printed name in parentheses) and any definition given. Unit: study. Axis labels and metrics used only for selection/tuning do not count (see rules).
items.performance.estimate: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset)] Every reported performance value. Value: list of rows {model, outcome, analysis (main | sensitivity | comparator | other), dataset_role (apparent | internal | external), dataset_or_split, subgroup, metric, value (printed), ci (printed or null), threshold (printed or null), evidence_id}. Include values in tables and figures (figure values only if printed in the figure; approximate readings are not estimates). Keep the main models' results apart from sensitivity analyses and comparator models with the analysis field; give the values in the rows, not as prose in this item.
items.performance.uncertainty: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset); 'all models' when shared] Core: whether uncertainty accompanies the performance estimates. Value per metric family: ci (method if stated, e.g. bootstrap 1,000, DeLong) | sd or range across folds/repeats, as printed. If estimates are printed without any CI, SD or range, status not_reported (values []); state 'point estimates only' in the rationale. Where some metrics have intervals and others not, give entries for those with intervals and '<metric> | none printed' for the others.
items.performance.dataset_role: [unit: study] Which dataset roles performance is reported for. Value: list of apparent | internal | external.
items.performance.threshold: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset); 'all models' when shared] Core: whether the classification threshold used for threshold-based metrics is reported. Two value entries per unit: '<unit> | method' (how chosen: 0.5 default, Youden, fixed sensitivity 80%, ... as printed, or 'not_reported') and '<unit> | value' (the printed threshold number, or 'not_reported'). Status reported when the method or the number is stated. not_applicable if no threshold-based metric (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, accuracy, F1) is reported (e.g. only AUROC and calibration).
items.performance.discrimination: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset)] Whether discrimination is reported (AUC/C-statistic). Value: reported (values in estimate rows) | not_reported. A ROC curve without a printed AUC value is not a reported discrimination value for that evaluation.
items.performance.calibration: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset)] Whether calibration is assessed (calibration plot, slope, intercept, Hosmer-Lemeshow, Brier as overall). Value: method as printed or not_reported.
items.performance.overall_error: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset)] Overall measures (Brier score, log loss, R2, RMSE/MAE for continuous outcomes). Value: printed metric names.
items.performance.classification_utility: [unit: evaluation (model x dataset)] Classification or utility metrics with printed values (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, accuracy, F1, decision curve/net benefit, clinical impact curve). Normalised names; axis labels do not count. The unit distinguishes the whole evaluation set from subgroups: values printed only for subgroups are entered with the subgroup in the unit, and the whole-set evaluation is then not_reported for those metrics.
items.intended_use.intended_use: [unit: study] The intended use stated (screening tool, risk identification, clinical decision support, understanding risk factors) and intended users. Value: printed phrase; judged only if clearly implied (say so).
items.presentation.model_presentation: [unit: model] How the final model is presented for use (equation, nomogram, score, web calculator, SHAP explanation only, none). Value: printed.
items.interpretation.interpretation_limitation: [unit: study] Limitations the authors state that concern the model (cross-sectional design, self-report, no external validation, generalisability). Value: list of stated limitations (short phrases).
items.funding.funding: [unit: study] Funding statement. Value: printed funder names or 'no funding' as stated.
items.conflicts.conflicts: [unit: study] Conflict of interest statement. Value: as stated.
items.predictors.outcome_overlap: [unit: study (or predictor group)] Whether any predictor is part of the outcome definition or directly derived from the values that define the outcome (e.g. appendicular lean mass and height as predictors of sarcopenia defined by ASM/height2; TyG index and triglyceride/glucose criteria of metabolic syndrome; anxiety outcome with closely related scales only if one is computed from the other). Value: none_found | overlap (predictor -> outcome component, with IDs) | possible (close proxy, not a component; say which). Facts only, no judgement of bias.
items.model_development.step_data_scope: [unit: model (or study when shared)] For each data-dependent step the report describes - imputation, scaling/normalisation, feature engineering, predictor selection, resampling for imbalance, hyperparameter tuning, model/algorithm selection, threshold selection, recalibration - which data it used, as stated: whole_dataset_before_split | training_only | within_cv_folds | test_outcomes_used (outcomes of a validation/test set used for tuning, choosing the algorithm, the number of predictors or the threshold, or recalibration, before performance on that set is reported) | external_predictors_transformed (a procedure fitted on development data applied to the predictors of a validation/external set: applying a training-fitted imputation model or scaler, harmonising variable coding, deriving variables such as PIR; this does not use outcomes and is not tuning) | not_stated. Keep fitting and application apart, e.g. {'imputation (fitting)': 'training_only', 'imputation (application to KNHANES)': 'external_predictors_transformed'}. Value: list {step: scope}. Facts only: when the report does not say when a step was done, the scope is not_stated (do not infer 'before split'). 'All data', 'the dataset' or 'the entire data' without reference to the split is not_stated (quote it in the rationale). No risk judgement.

note: v3 after the pilot review (internal review note, 2026-11-16): reporting status separated from internal inconsistency; fixed unit of extraction per item; no unsupported inference; metric normalisation; availability, outcome overlap and leakage separated; extraction kept factual (methodological appraisal such as leakage risk is left to the later risk-of-bias assessment). | v3.1 after the review of the v3 pilot (prompt_148, 2026-11-17): status follows the item's core question with partly reported details kept as separate value entries; not_applicable narrowed for validation items; statements of absence only when printed; one canonical unit label; value kind per value; text of another version of the report is outside the coded report. | v3.1.1 (prompt_149 review of the v3.1 pilot; small amendment, no redesign): the three rule questions settled conditionally (no validation data -> not_applicable except validation.type 'no validation'; a step not done counts as reported only when statements establish it, absence of a value does not; data scope only when the cited statements name the step and its data); step_data_scope separates use of test outcomes from applying development-fitted procedures to external predictors; kind judged for categories assigned from printed text; uncertainty with point estimates only = not_reported. | v3.1.2 (prompt_150 review; final, frozen for the full coding): dataset_linkage = pooling or record linkage only (separate external validation data are not linkage); availability_at_use = final-model inputs only; inconsistency only for the same object and condition (different statistical units, naming or explainable analysis differences excluded); performance rows carry analysis = main | sensitivity | comparator | other; partial values never turn an answered item into not_reported. | v3.1.3 (prompt_151): one sentence of rule 4 made consistent with rule 2 (printed part + derived addition = reported); frozen for the full coding.
